record.original_question: For every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed convex sets in the plane, is there an element C in F and a straight line l such that l separates C from at least floor(n/3) up to an additive constant c other elements of F, where separating two convex sets means they lie in opposite open half-planes determined by l?

evidence.quote: we say that a line l separates them if the convex sets are such that one is contained in each of the open half-planes defined by l.
Conjecture 4 Any family F of n disjoint closed convex sets has an element that can be separated with a single line from at least b n 3 c ± c elements of F.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let F = {C_1, ..., C_n} be a family of n pairwise disjoint closed convex sets in the Euclidean plane R^2. Say that a straight line l separates two convex sets A, B ⊂ R^2 if A and B lie in the two distinct open half-planes determined by l (so neither set meets l). 

Prove or disprove the following: there exists an absolute constant c ≥ 0 such that for every such family F there exist an element C ∈ F and a straight line l with the property that l separates C from at least ⌊n/3⌋ − c of the remaining elements of F.
artifact.category_tag: Discrete and combinatorial geometry — separation of convex sets
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (that for n pairwise disjoint planar convex sets some element can be separated by a single line from ≈ n/3 of the others) appears to remain open in full generality. Partial results are known: for disks, a separation of about (n−7)/4 elements is achievable; for line segments that can be extended to pairwise disjoint half-lines, a bound of ⌈n/3⌉+1 has been established. No proof or counterexample for arbitrary convex sets achieving the n/3 bound has been found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Separating convex sets in the plane
status_evidence.snippet: For n disjoint line segments extendable to disjoint semilines, a line separates one segment from at least ⌈n/3⌉+1 others; results for disks give (n−7)/4.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases (segments, disks) of the n/3 separation conjecture are known; the general case is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Tangencies between families of disjoint regions in the plane (Pach)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys related separation/tangency problems for disjoint convex regions in the plane.
status_evidence.claim: Related separation problems for disjoint convex regions remain an active topic without a known general n/3 separation theorem.
